source: Grierson, Linguistic Survey of India, Volume IV: Munda and Dravidian Languages (1906), Kōḍā or Kōṛā section; Birbhum specimen prepared by Rev. P. O. Bodding (1903)
edition: Original 1906 Calcutta printing, not a later reprint
rights: Public domain original (1906); Wikimedia Commons public-domain scan. Only two public-domain printed page images and factual transcriptions are packaged; the 701-page DjVu is a local cache.
scope: Directly glossed simplex Birbhum Koda examples in editorial phonology/grammar prose, printed pp. 109-110 (DjVu pages 128-129); 20 candidate form-gloss examples individually inventoried.
excluded_scope: Printed pp. 107-108 are ethnographic and classification context, not a lexical table.
Complex, inflected, sentence, and paradigm examples on printed pp. 109-110 are context only, not split into inferred lemmas.
Birbhum interlinear prodigal-son narrative on printed pp. 111-113 is excluded wholesale; its word-by-word translation is not treated as independent lexical elicitation.
Dhaṅgār comparison on printed p. 114 is another named lect, not Birbhum Koda.

Bankura prose/examples on printed p. 114 and its interlinear specimen on p. 115 are excluded wholesale: Grierson calls the Bankura specimen very corrupt and says he reconstructed its opening without consistently restoring the semiconsonants.
source_text_method: Visually read public-domain scanned pages; English Tesseract OCR compared but not used as authority for diacritics. Each installed form manually checked against the print.
lect: Koda base language, source-qualified Birbhum dialect; no exact coordinate supplied
etymology: No graph edges. Grierson groups numerals six and above as Aryan loanwords without naming source word forms; that prose is retained as source context, not a donor edge.
overlap: Existing compiled Koda has 620 rows, mainly Kim et al. 2010 Bangladesh survey. The five selected forms have zero exact form-plus-gloss overlaps against those 620 rows; later survey has comparable numeral forms, but no known reproduction of this Bodding 1903 Birbhum specimen. See overlap-review.json. Parallel source citations are preserved.
